name: Athenian selection of public officers by lot
description: In mid-fifth-century Athens, citizen assemblies voted and public officers, including council members and jurors, were chosen by lot.

date.label: by approximately the mid-fifth century BCE
date.basis: The retrospective museum history says by the mid-fifth century BCE; -450 is an approximate indexing anchor, not an introduction date.

events.statement: By the mid-fifth century BCE, Athenian citizen officials, councillors and jurors were selected by lot and received public pay.
events.scope: The museum overview retrospectively describes practices in use by mid-century, not a surviving contemporary document or the introduction of every practice. Citizenship excluded most residents; the overview simplifies the varying rules for different offices.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 15, historical overview of mid-fifth-century Athens
evidence.supports: The museum’s overview describes selection by lot, public payment and citizen assembly rights by the mid-fifth century BCE.

contributions.resource: Held civic office, sat as jurors or councillors, and participated in assemblies.

evidence.locator: Printed p. 15, historical overview of mid-fifth-century Athens
evidence.supports: The museum’s overview describes selection by lot, public payment and citizen assembly rights by the mid-fifth century BCE.

earliest_record.rationale: Earliest episode established in this source-based account; not a claim of origin or global priority.

caveats: The date range represents an approximate mid-century description, not the introduction of each practice. Political citizenship excluded most residents, including women, enslaved people and resident noncitizens.
